ios.desc:
PhotoCraft is an AI-powered photo editing app designed to help you create stunning images effortlessly. Whether you want to enhance portraits, generate artistic avatars, or improve photo quality, PhotoCraft makes it simple and fast.

KEY FEATURES
• AI Photo Enhancer – Improve clarity, lighting, and overall quality
• AI Portrait & Avatar Generator – Create realistic and artistic portraits
• Face Enhancement – Smooth skin, sharpen details, and enhance facial features
• Background Tools – Remove or replace backgrounds easily
• High-Quality Exports – Save images in high resolution
• Simple & Intuitive UI – No editing skills required

SUBSCRIPTIONS & PURCHASES
PhotoCraft offers auto-renewable subscriptions and a lifetime purchase option to unlock premium features.

Subscription plans automatically renew unless canceled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Payment is charged to your Apple ID account. You can manage or cancel subscriptions in your Apple ID settings after purchase.

WHY PHOTOGRAPHERS & CREATORS LOVE PHOTOCRAFT
• Fast AI processing
• Professional-quality results
• Clean and easy-to-use interface
• Regular improvements and updates

Download PhotoCraft today and turn your photos into stunning visuals using AI.

show_hn.title: Show HN: PhotoCraft – an AI photo editor I built and shipped as my first iOS app

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I’m an indie developer and I recently shipped my first iOS app, PhotoCraft. It’s an AI-powered photo editor focused on enhancement, avatars, and creative edits.

This project started mainly as a way for me to learn how to take an idea all the way from development to passing App Store review and shipping something real. The hardest parts for me weren’t the models or the UI, but scope control, onboarding decisions, and dealing with review feedback.

A few things I learned along the way:

“Good enough to ship” is harder to define than expected

App Store rejections are more about clarity and UX than code

Cutting features early saved me a lot of time later

I’m sharing this mostly to get feedback from people who’ve built and shipped products before. I’d especially appreciate thoughts on:

First-time user experience

Whether the feature set feels focused or bloated

Monetization flow (what feels fair vs frustrating)

Happy to answer any questions about the build, tooling, or App Store review process.

Thanks for taking a look.

— Deva
